text: To peddle is to sell by promoting, often goods of doubtful value. Influencers peddle elixirs whose benefits are not proven.
An evangelist eagerly spreads a belief, hoping to convert others. Bryan Johnson loudly urges people to adopt his anti-ageing routine.
Arduous means demanding great effort and time, like climbing a steep mountain. Proving a drug slows ageing takes years of trials.
Longevity means a long life. A longevity clinic sells treatments that promise more years, or healthier ones.
Posh means rich and fashionable. Chelsea is an expensive area of London.
To reside is to live in a place. The clinic is based on a quiet street in Chelsea.
Cryotherapy means exposing the body to extreme cold, here -110°C, for a few minutes. Fans say it invigorates; strong evidence is thin.
Invigorated means filled with energy and freshness. The man says so himself, which is not the same as proof.
A hyperbaric chamber is a sealed capsule with air pressure above normal, in which people breathe pure oxygen. Doctors use it for conditions like diving sickness.
Intravenous means given directly into a vein, usually through a drip.
NAD+ is a molecule cells use to turn food into energy. Its levels fall with age, which is why it is sold as a supplement, though studies are inconclusive.
Ozone is a form of oxygen with three atoms. Mixing it into blood is an unproven treatment.
To garner is to gather or earn. The quest to live forever has gathered fresh interest.
Lifespan is how long a person or creature lives.
A counterpart holds an equivalent role elsewhere. Sam Altman runs OpenAI, a rival to Mr Amodei's Anthropic.
Overheard means heard by chance. Two leaders were caught on a microphone discussing immortality.
An organ transplant replaces a failing organ with a healthy donor's. The leaders mused that swapping organs repeatedly might extend life.
To muse is to think or speak thoughtfully, often idly, about a possibility.
Chronic means lasting a long time or constantly returning, as with long-term diseases.
To seep is to flow slowly through small gaps. Interest in living longer is slowly spreading into ordinary life.
The mainstream is what ordinary people accept, as opposed to fringe ideas.
The OECD is a club of mostly rich countries that shares economic data and policy. Its members have ageing populations.
A regime here means a strict routine, like a diet or exercise plan. Mr Johnson follows a famously extreme one.
To seize on something is to grab it eagerly. Two industries want to profit from the longevity trend.
Dubious means doubtful or not to be trusted. These treatments have little proof behind them.
Efficacy is how well something works at doing what it claims.
Drugmakers are pharmaceutical companies.
Biotechs are small companies using biology to develop medicines. Big drugmakers often partner with them.
The point is to treat the process of getting old, not just single diseases that come with it.
A niche market is a small, specialised group of customers. Pharma bosses once thought obesity was one.
GLP-1s are a class of drugs, first for diabetes, then weight loss. Their huge sales changed what drugmakers think is possible.
$1trn means one trillion dollars, a thousand billion. Eli Lilly was the first drugmaker worth that much.
The bloom of youth is the fresh, healthy look of being young. It is the section title's playful nod to what customers want.
Impatient people will not wait. Here, customers want results before real medicines exist.
To cater to someone is to supply what they want.
Genome sequencing reads a person's complete set of DNA to look for risks.
An autoimmune disorder is one where the immune system attacks the body's own healthy cells.
Symptoms are signs of illness a patient can notice, like pain or fever.
An MRI scan uses magnets and radio waves to make detailed images of the inside of the body.
A subscription is a regular payment for ongoing service, here repeated health tests.
To be backed by someone is to be funded and supported by them.
Loosely defined means no firm rules say what counts, so any clinic can use the label.
This simile says patients choose medical treatments casually, like picking a pizza topping, instead of being guided by a doctor.
Adventurous means willing to take risks.
Experimental treatments are not yet proven safe or effective.
Stem cells can grow into many types of cell. Clinics inject them hoping to repair tissue; most such uses are unproven.
An elixir is a magical-sounding potion said to cure or prolong life.
Peptides are short chains of amino acids, the building blocks of proteins. Some are sold as injections with big claims.
Tendons are tough cords connecting muscle to bone.
Cost-effective means worth the money because benefits outweigh costs.
Over-diagnosis means finding conditions that would never have caused harm, leading to needless worry and tests.
An anomaly is something unusual. Most are harmless.
Inconclusive means the evidence does not settle the question either way.
A wild west is a place with few rules, like the old American frontier.
An anecdote is a personal story, weaker evidence than a controlled study.
To dodge is to avoid. Sellers label peptides 'for research use only' to escape regulation.
Approval is official permission to sell a medicine, given after trials show it is safe and works.
A placebo is a dummy treatment given to a comparison group, so scientists can tell what the real drug adds.
Preliminary means early and subject to change.
A yardstick is a standard used to measure or judge something.
To re-establish is to bring something back. GLP-1s showed big profits in mass-market drugs again.
Risk appetite is how much uncertainty a company will accept. Pharma firms like large markets they understand.
A consultancy is a firm that sells expert advice to companies.
Buying an option is paying for the right, but not the duty, to acquire something later. Drugmakers can pick up a biotech's drug if it works.
A startup is a young company, often betting on a new idea.
Therapeutics are treatments or medicines for disease.
Idiopathic means with no known cause.
Pulmonary fibrosis is a disease where lung tissue becomes scarred and stiff, making breathing hard.
A late-stage trial tests a drug on many patients, the last step before approval.
Epigenetic reprogramming means resetting the chemical switches on DNA that control which genes are on, aiming to make old cells act young.
To reverse is to make something go backwards, here, undoing ageing instead of just slowing it.
Muddled means confused or mixed up.
Here it means early longevity ventures failed to deliver.
Resveratrol is a compound in red wine once hoped to slow ageing.
To lay off workers is to dismiss them, usually because the company cannot afford them.
To accelerate is to speed up.
